ALL 6 TABLES: ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; 30 policies total, every one role-scoped (pg_policies roles = '{public}' returns 0 rows); zero policies reference has_role
decisions: content_json / layout_config: grepped all of src/ - ZERO matches. Migration 20260212090000 (which added them, and which import.sql replays) was authored locally and never applied live; types.ts does not declare them either. All three sources agree, so they are omitted. Neither column is in my scope's tables anyway, but the grep result is reported for the essays owner.

Admin writes INLINE the user_roles EXISTS check everywhere; has_role() is never referenced by any policy in this section. Proven, not assumed: I stood up a local Postgres 16, applied a stubbed Supabase prelude + this section, then REVOKEd EXECUTE ON has_role FROM anon, authenticated, PUBLIC - reproducing failure (a) - and ran the full acceptance suite. Every assertion still passed.

DISCOVERED DEPENDENCY that the inline pattern rests on: a sub-select inside a policy IS subject to the target table's own RLS. With RLS on user_roles and no readable SELECT policy, every admin INSERT failed with 'new row violates row-level security policy'. The pattern only works because 20251223113138 gives user_roles a 'Users can view their own roles' FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id) policy plus table-level SELECT to authenticated. Documented in a prominent SQL comment; the user_roles owner must not drop or narrow that policy to admins-only.

finance_models anon SELECT is gated USING (is_published = true) rather than the original USING (true). Same class as failure (b): the table has an is_published flag, useFinanceModels already filters .eq('is_published', true), and USING (true) would leak unpublished models through PostgREST. Admin preview still works because useFinanceModelBySlug does not filter is_published and the authenticated policy allows published OR admin. Verified: anon sees only the published row; a non-admin authenticated user sees only the published row; admin sees both.

finance_modules.track_slug FK -> finance_sections(slug) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT. CASCADE on update because these slugs have already been renamed once in production (planning-forecasting -> planning, financial-analytics -> analytics) and a future rename must propagate rather than orphan modules. RESTRICT on delete because the 4 tracks are fixed navigation entry points - dropping one out from under its modules is an error to surface, not to cascade into silent content loss. Both behaviours tested.

fsli_sections.page_slug FK -> fsli_pages(slug) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE. The original 20251223120457 had NO foreign key at all - this strengthens it. CASCADE on delete is forced by actual usage: useUnifiedContent.ts:290 deletes fsli_pages rows directly, and with RESTRICT/NO ACTION that admin delete would start failing on the constraint. Tested: deleting a page removes its sections.

Split read/write policies with explicit TO anon / TO authenticated on all 30, no FOR ALL anywhere. FOR ALL would also have quietly failed the fsli_sections upsert path, since the original FOR ALL policies carried a USING clause but no WITH CHECK.

Both admin INSERT and admin UPDATE policies on fsli_sections are load-bearing: FsliSection.tsx:49 and FsliContentSection.tsx:58 upsert with onConflict 'page_slug,section_key', which PostgREST compiles to INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. Tested by running the upsert twice as admin (insert then update -> content = v2) and once as a non-admin (denied).

Explicit table-level GRANTs (SELECT to anon; SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE to authenticated) rather than relying on Supabase's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES. A missing grant is the other mechanism by which a public page dies with 'permission denied', and it makes the baseline self-sufficient if applied by a role other than postgres. RLS, not the grant, gates rows. Side benefit: anon writes are refused at the privilege layer ('permission denied for table') before RLS is even consulted.

finance_settings seeds BOTH keys. useUpdateFinanceSetting (useFinance.ts:92) issues a bare UPDATE ... WHERE key = $1 - never an upsert - so a missing row makes the admin editor report success while saving nothing. featured_finance_essay_id seeds as NULL because it stores an essays.id and every essay UUID is regenerated by the rebuild.

Dropped the original's redundant idx_finance_modules_slug (20260220181848): the UNIQUE constraint on slug already provides that index. Kept the (track_slug, sort_order) composite, which matches the track-listing query. Added idx_finance_models_published_order (is_published, sort_order) to match useFinanceModels' only list query.

finance_sections seeded with the FINAL 4 slugs (fundamentals, strategic-finance, planning, analytics) and the post-20260220_001 production descriptions/icons. Deliberately did NOT seed the 32 finance_modules rows, the fsli_pages rows, or any finance_models rows - see open_risks.

essays-side columns (fsli_slug, module_id, finance_section, lesson_type) are referenced only in comments; I authored no column outside my 6 tables. Confirmed no finance_fundamentals or tracker table is created or referenced.

open_risks: CONTENT NOT SEEDED, by design: the 32 finance_modules rows (final state in supabase/migrations/_archive/20260220_001_fix_production_finance_data.sql, STEP 4), the 24 fsli_pages rows (20251223120457_1f1d9359-ac71-46c3-893a-372a54b27a3e.sql), and all finance_models rows. Until they are loaded, /finance/:track, /accounting/fsli and /finance-in-action render empty. The orchestrator's brief specified seeding only for finance_sections' final slug set and finance_settings' NULL featured id, so I kept the rest as a separate data-restore step. If curriculum content should ship inside the baseline, say so and I will lift those INSERTs verbatim - they are all slug-keyed, so no UUID regeneration problem.

RESTORE ORDER now matters for FSLI: fsli_sections.page_slug is a real FK (the original had none), so fsli_pages must be loaded before fsli_sections or the inserts fail. Any historical fsli_sections row whose page_slug has no matching fsli_pages row will be rejected rather than silently imported as an orphan - worth a pre-import check against the old dump if one exists.

CROSS-SECTION DEPENDENCY, highest risk item: public.user_roles MUST keep 'Users can view their own roles' FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id) (from 20251223113138) plus table-level SELECT to authenticated. A policy sub-select is subject to the target table's RLS, so if that policy is dropped or narrowed to admin-only, all 20 admin-write policies in this section evaluate FALSE and admins lose write access with a misleading 'violates row-level security policy' error. I reproduced this failure in testing. Whoever owns the user_roles section needs to know.

The 'finance-models' storage bucket and its storage.objects policies are NOT created here (storage is outside my table scope). ModelAdminPanel.tsx:46 uploads xlsx to it and stores the public URL in finance_models.excel_file_url; without the bucket, uploads fail and existing excel_file_url links 404. Note that 20260622135932 also replaced the public-read policy on that bucket with an admin-only listing policy - decide deliberately which of those two states the baseline ships.

finance_models anon reads are now gated on is_published, a deliberate behaviour change from the live USING (true). If any public route is expected to show an unpublished model, this will present as a 404 for anonymous visitors.

types.ts reports Relationships: [] for finance_modules even though 20260218_001 and 20260220_001 both declare the track_slug FK, and it still lists essays_fundamental_id_fkey for a column 20260218_003 dropped - so that file's relationship metadata is a stale snapshot and I trusted the migrations plus src usage for FK shape instead. No src consumer uses a PostgREST embedded resource across finance_modules -> finance_sections, so adding the FK cannot break an existing nested select.
Validation was done on PostgreSQL 16.13 (the only server binary available locally), not 17. Nothing in this DDL is version-sensitive, but the apply itself has not been run against the real project.

finance_models.module_references is uuid[] and cannot carry a foreign key, so it can go stale silently after a module delete. Consumers resolve ids against the module list client-side and render nothing for a miss - acceptable, but a periodic integrity sweep would catch drift.
